data.description: Inputs that must be refused, never loaded. Each case feeds one event stream to the reference implementation (tools/reference.py) and passes only if the engine raises a refusal carrying the case's expectedRefusalCode. A refused stream produces no ledger at all - fail closed - so a malformed date can never fall through a string comparison into 'saved', and a negative outcome can never be laundered into positive grams. A missing key or an explicit null is the only way to leave a date unset (model.md section 1). The validator (tools/validate.py) runs this suite and refuses the run if any case loads.

cases.description: event date with a leading space; naive string compare reads it as on-or-before the use-by and would claim the grams as saved
cases.proves: a malformed 'on' is refused, never compared as a raw string, never treated as absent

cases.description: event date year 0000: correct shape, impossible calendar year, and sorts before every real date under string compare
cases.proves: shape alone is not enough - the calendar date must be real

cases.description: unpadded month and day (2026-1-5): loose date parsing must not let it through
cases.proves: only strict zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD is well-formed

cases.description: use-by month 13: well-formed shape, impossible month
cases.proves: a malformed lotUseBy is refused even though the event date is fine

cases.description: use-by day 30 in February: well-formed shape, impossible calendar day
cases.proves: impossible calendar days are refused, not silently normalized

cases.description: empty-string event date: sorts before every real date under string compare and would claim saved
cases.proves: an empty string is malformed input, not an absent date - it must fail loudly, never load as nil

cases.description: timestamp instead of a date (2026-10-01T14:00:00): dates are local calendar dates only
cases.proves: datetime strings are refused; only exact YYYY-MM-DD loads

cases.description: event date as a number (20261002) instead of a string
cases.proves: a non-string date is malformed input, not a compact ISO form

cases.description: negative consumption outcome: dates and use-by would make it saved, but a negative outcome is a data error, not savings
cases.proves: a negative consume outcome can never be classified as saved; there is no absolute-value laundering
negative waste is likewise refused, not flipped positive
a negative write-off is a data error, never a counted outcome

cases.description: negative adjust delta: the contract carries the delta's magnitude, so a signed delta must not slip through as an inventory correction
cases.proves: negative deltas are refused on correction events too
zero never loads as a silent no-op outcome; the contract says positive
a negative intake is a data error on intake events too
